methods.label: Find the base using the strip's perpendicular width
methods.explanation:
Each strip is bounded by two parallel lines, so their overlap is a parallelogram. Choose its horizontal bottom side as the base, and call its length \(b\). The corresponding height is the horizontal strip's width, \(1\), so the area is \(b\).

To find \(b\), call the left and right endpoints of this base \(P\) and \(Q\). Draw a perpendicular from \(P\) to the slanted boundary through \(Q\), meeting it at \(T\). The slanted strip has perpendicular width \(1\), so \(PT=1\).

The marked angle \(\alpha\) is obtuse. Set \(\beta=180^\circ-\alpha\), the acute angle \(PQT\). In right triangle \(PQT\), the hypotenuse is \(PQ=b\), so
\[
\sin\beta=\frac{PT}{PQ}=\frac1b.
\]
Supplementary angles have equal sines, hence \(\sin\beta=\sin\alpha\), giving
\[
\text{Area}=b\cdot1=\frac1{\sin\alpha}.
\]
The crossing strips give \(0<\alpha<180^\circ\), so \(\sin\alpha>0\) and division is valid. The answer is \(\boxed{\frac1{\sin\alpha}}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
